title: We made a puzzle game with AI agents in four days
author: ronedgecomb
selftext:
Our team directed and playtested [Pulled Apart](https://ronedgecomb.itch.io/pulled-apart) for the [2026 Epic AI MegaJam](https://itch.io/jam/2026-epic-ai-megajam). A main Claude Code agent built the game in Unreal, with subagents helping with art, animation, sound, and reviews.

In the first build, you could throw a hand at a lever, leave a foot on a pressure plate, and roll your head through a gap. It was fun, but I played through the whole thing in a minute or two. For the last act, we made the robot you rescue playable. Its little blue cart could roll onto truck scales the first robot was too light to trigger, so the two robots had to help each other get out.

If you've built a game with agents, what did your first full playthrough make you change?

[Free Windows build on itch.io](https://ronedgecomb.itch.io/pulled-apart) \- [One-minute gameplay on YouTube](https://youtu.be/xZYJgU-Hgrc) \- [Full devlog](https://ronedgecomb.dev/projects/pulled-apart/)
